d.d: An additional piece of information, an addition to existing information.
d.x: I just made an update to my blog about my trip to Rome.

d.d: An advisement providing more up-to-date information than currently known.
d.x: He gave me an update on the situation in New York.

d.d: A modification of something to a more recent, up-to-date version; (in software) a minor upgrade.
d.x: Our database receives an update every morning at 3 AM.

d.d: To bring (a thing) up to date.
d.x: I need to update my records to take account of the most recent transaction.

d.d: To bring (a person) up to date: to inform (a person) about recent developments.
d.x: Update me on what happened while I was away.

d.d: To change one's credence in a proposition in response to new evidence.
d.x: I need to update on the new data.
